question: Does TensorLBM's port of the open-source wall-order-parameter (ghost-layer order-parameter) wetting route reproduce the equilibrium contact angle implied by the same free energy, within the owner's 15 % bar?

oss_files: lattice_boltzmann/validation.py (wettability block: psi_wall_list ghost rows; getNabla_psi* isotropic 9-point stencils; getMu; getgeq; getLarge_F; halfway_bounceback)
reference.oss_license: no LICENSE file in the repository -> no verbatim vendoring; only the method (ghost-layer wall order parameter) is transplanted and described
reference.oss_provenance: platform OSS inventory (oss_solutions, Fingering_dynamics) + source line list recorded by the round-0 deliverable; the reference script was executed out-of-tree (provenance note in the report, section 1) and its own integration diverged (psi NaN at step 200), so it produced no usable angle -> the acceptance gate cannot rest on it (honest limitation, reported)
reference.analytic_anchor: cos(theta) = (3 psi_w - psi_w^3)/2, derived independently in the report section 2 from the truncated tanh profile of the same free energy (energy difference of the two wall-wetted bulk phases / sigma)

predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: a KPI is xi-converged when |theta(xi2)-theta(xi3)|/theta(xi3) < 10 %; the xi = 3 value is the reported one
predeclared_thresholds.stationarity_rule: the port arm reports max|psi(t)-psi(t-check_every)| at the end of the run; the angle is accepted as a *static* value only together with the degeneracy flag below
predeclared_thresholds.measurement_validity_rule: the area/height cap inversion is valid only when layer_area_per_column * nx / area < 0.5 (the equilibrium wall adsorption layer must not absorb the drop). Runs violating it are reported, flagged cap_measurable=false, and excluded from the acceptance gate with the mechanism recorded (never silently dropped, never tuned)
predeclared_thresholds.stability_rule: a run producing non-finite fields is reported as failed, not restarted with different parameters

validated_window.justification: the wall adsorption-layer capacity (layer_area_per_column) stays below 20 % of the drop area for |psi_w| <= 0.5 and exceeds 99 % at psi_w = +0.70, where no cap exists any more (measured, see summary.json layer_capacity)

metrics.theta_deg: port arm: excess-area/apex-height inversion of the Laplace cap relation A/h^2 = (th - sin th cos th)/(1-cos th)^2 (primary); circle fit of the level set (secondary, ill-conditioned for shallow caps and reported as such)
metrics.theta_cac_deg: cac arm: median of the circle fit and spherical-cap inversion of tensorlbm.wetting.metrics (independent measurement code that never sees the solver's internal angle)

unit_of_analysis: one static equilibration at fixed (psi_w, xi, box) / one CAC run at fixed (psi_w, steps)

baseline_control.baseline: analytic Young law of the same free energy (section 2 derivation)
baseline_control.control: psi_w = 0 (neutral wall) must give 90 deg; the xi ladder {2,3,4} and the box ladder {80x56, 160x100} isolate resolution from model error
baseline_control.independent_arm: cac arm: separate solver + separate order parameter + separate measurement toolbox

variables_controlled: free energy a(psi^2-1)^2/4, kappa = 3 sigma xi/4
wall ghost rows at y=-1 and y=ny
confounders: the analytic anchor shares the free energy with the model: it is a consistency check, not an experiment (honest limitation; the independent arm is the CAC solver)
the OSS reference itself produced no number (NaN), so the OSS-vs-port numeric comparison is WITHHELD, not passed
interface width xi is a model parameter, so xi -> 0 extrapolation would be needed for a sharp-interface anchor; the xi ladder is reported instead
stopping_rule: fixed iteration cap 30000 for every port run; no run extended or truncated after inspecting the angle
